newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
U.S. First Lady Rodham Hillary Clinton has prasied the family planning and rural development activities in Bangladesh.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made a passionate appeal to all to take a pivotal step for a poverty-free globe as world leaders began a summit here on Sunday with the goal of providing small loans to 100 million poor people.
About 15 million people in Bangladesh are at risk of arsenic contamination, according to a recent survey.
Nearly 100 people, including seven policemen, were injured in a clash between police and workers of a jute mills in Comilla district.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Monday accused the ruling Awami League of running the government in autocratic style in the name of national consensus.

Ion Cernivcean, head of a visiting Romanian trade delegation, said on Monday that Bangladesh had the ample scope for exporting pharmaceuticals, knitwear, frozen foods and agriculture product to the East European country.
The on-going negotiation between Dhaka and Kuala Lampur in Malaysian capital on the illegal immigrant issue would yield a positive outcome, a senior foreign ministry official said.
